lifecycle.creation_reason: Found and MEASURED while proving MT-116 PT-116-1 on 2026-08-12. It is a DIFFERENT defect from the one MT-116 fixed (spec-size vs paint-size mismatch), it is not covered by the MT-116 pixel guard, and fixing it would have been an unscoped product change. Deferred here per the Operator standing rule rather than absorbed or lost.

scope.summary: Make the wikilink chip label wrap the same way its galley does, so a long chip inside a narrow reading column cannot paint outside the column with a mis-sized pill behind it.

defect_detail.mechanism: The chip label is drawn with a single painter.text call, which NEVER WRAPS. The galley that measures the chip DOES wrap. When the label is long enough to need two rows, chip_rect_for_span unions the two galley rows into one tall pill while the painted text runs off in a single line.
defect_detail.measured_evidence: At editor font size 20.0 with a 46-character H1 label, the painted label ran 325px PAST the 720pt reading column while chip_rect_for_span produced a single 88px-tall pill. Measured during MT-116 proof authoring, not inferred.
defect_detail.why_MT116_does_not_cover_it: MT-116 fixed the pill/label FONT METRIC mismatch (the pill measured at the user-configured style size, the label painted at a hardcoded 15.0 constant). This is a WRAPPING mismatch and survives that fix. The MT-116 pixel guard deliberately REJECTS such a configuration as unmeasurable via a pill-height check rather than asserting on it, so this defect is explicitly outside its coverage.
defect_detail.related_finding_headings_at_default_size: The MT-116 record claimed no behavioural change at the default editor size 15.0. That holds for PARAGRAPHS only. An H1 at editor 15.0 resolves to style size 27.0 through HEADING_SCALE, so heading chips DID change at the default size - the H1 before-frame differs between the fixed and reverted builds (936004... vs c72f4f...). Recorded here so the next implementer does not trust the paragraph-only claim for headings.

acceptance_criteria: AC-124-1: a chip label long enough to wrap paints INSIDE the reading column, and the pill drawn behind it matches the rows the label actually occupies. Neither may be measured by a different rule than the other.

AC-124-2: proven by direct frame inspection at a magnification where the label is legible - the frame must be OPENED and described, not merely captured. State the exact editor font size, block kind, and id length tested.

AC-124-3: a non-vacuous painted-output guard, in the style MT-116 established: it must go RED when the wrapping fix is reverted. Beware the two near-vacuous traps MT-116 hit and documented - antialiased pill-corner ring counted as label ink, and a 3-pixel underline remnant holding the ink bounding box full-width.
AC-124-4: the MT-116 pixel guard must be extended or a sibling added so this configuration is ASSERTED rather than rejected as unmeasurable by its pill-height check.
AC-124-5: heading chips are covered explicitly at the DEFAULT editor size, because HEADING_SCALE means headings are already off-default there.
AC-124-6: no regression to the MT-034, MT-042, MT-068 and MT-074 chip surfaces, which share this line-layout code.
proof_targets: PT-124-1: a mounted GPU frame at a wrapping configuration, OPENED and described, showing label and pill agreeing inside the reading column.
PT-124-2: the guard shown RED with the fix reverted and GREEN with it applied, both outputs captured verbatim.
PT-124-3: before/after frame sha256 pairs proving the frames are not byte-identical (the render_proof_frame preceding-frame hazard recorded as PT-116-3).
scope.risk_if_missed: A long wikilink chip in a heading or a narrow column paints outside the reading column onto the page, which is operator-visible corruption of the document surface rather than a cosmetic pill mismatch.

gui_obligation.requirement: Argus/mounted GPU frame evidence, opened and described, at a wrapping configuration.

user_manual_obligation.requirement: NOT_APPLICABLE unless the wrapping affordance changes documented editor behaviour.

hbr_obligations.VIS: Painted-output proof required; a compile or a spec-value assertion is not acceptance. MT-116 proved a spec-only guard cannot detect a paint-site defect.
hbr_obligations.INT: HBR-INT-009: Flight Recorder NOT_APPLICABLE (no business event); internal_diagnostics and Palmistry DEFERRED-with-reason while unshipped per CX-981-005.
